title: MEDIA-INTEL
universal_lens: The media-intel layer formalizes the NFL betting ecosystem as a continuous-time Markov decision process. Agents update latent power ratings via Bayesian inference from play-by-play data, projecting truncated distributions over player props and season-long futures to identify arbitrage against market-implied priors.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps podcast transcripts and analyst newsletters into a hierarchical Bayesian network. Play-level EPA models serve as likelihood functions updating team strength priors. Conformal prediction intervals bound projected win totals, quantifying epistemic uncertainty across varying data granularities.
gse_mapping: GSE translates dynamic uncertainty modeling into discrete state transitions. Weekly rating updates act as stochastic kernels shifting the probability mass over future game states. Truncated yardage distributions inform situational reasoning for in-game prop adjustments.

primitives.name: Dynamic Uncertainty Simulator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Podcast: Apple Podcasts "Sharp Football Analysis by Warren Sharp" — charts every preseason week offense/defense data (shotgun rate, motion, personnel groupings).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: P(S_t | S_{t-1}): Conditional probability of state at time t given previous state, dimensionless. \theta_t: Vector of updated power ratings, dimensionless.
primitives.assumptions: Team performance evolves as a Markovian process; weekly updates fully capture relevant information shifts without hidden confounders.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Fails during extreme regime shifts (e.g., catastrophic QB injuries) where historical transition matrices no longer approximate future dynamics.

layer2.mapping: Maps directly to GSE's Monte Carlo season simulators that integrate power ratings with injury probabilities to price futures.
layer2.telemetry: Variance reduction in projected win totals after weekly simulation runs.

primitives.name: Truncated Prop Distributions
primitives.verbatim_quote: ### Establish The Run (ETR) — establishtherun.com - Who: Adam Levitan + Evan Silva (renowned fantasy experts).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Y: Random variable for receiving yards, measured in yards. f(y): Probability density function, dimensionless per yard. y_min: Lower truncation bound (0 yards).
primitives.assumptions: Player output is bounded below by zero and exhibits heavy right-tails, violating standard Gaussian assumptions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down when assuming normality for mean vs. median calculations, leading to systematic mispricing of high-variance receiver props.

layer2.mapping: Derives the exact PDF kernel used in GSI's conformal inference modules for player-specific market edge detection.
layer2.telemetry: Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic comparing empirical yardage distributions against fitted truncated models.

primitives.name: EPA Likelihood Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Methodology bent: Play-level EPA models, situational statistics, context-heavy (not pure betting); Baldwin uses expected points / passing efficiency frameworks.
primitives.latex: EPA(\Delta d, s) = P(score|\Delta d, s) \cdot V(score) - P(TD|d,s)
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \Delta d: Change in distance to goal, yards. s: Down and distance state tuple, dimensionless. V(score): Expected point value of scoring, dimensionless.
primitives.assumptions: Expected points are additive and stationary across different game script contexts and field positions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs near the end of halves/games where 'garbage time' alters optimal play-calling and invalidates standard EPA valuations.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to the core situational valuation engine in GSE, providing the ground-truth reward function for reinforcement learning agents.
layer2.telemetry: Correlation between aggregated play-level EPA and actual point differential.

reasoning_traces.think:
The extraction of sovereign primitives from the media-intel census requires isolating the underlying mathematical operators driving modern NFL analytics. First, the dynamic uncertainty simulator acts as a temporal evolution operator. By treating team strength as a latent variable updated weekly via Bayesian conditioning on new play-by-play data, we construct a Markov chain over the state space of all 32 teams. This allows for the projection of season-long futures through Monte Carlo integration. Second, the truncated prop distribution primitive addresses the non-Gaussian nature of individual player outputs. Standard normal approximations fail to capture the hard boundary at zero and the long right-tail of explosive plays. Modeling these as truncated or skewed distributions provides a rigorous foundation for pricing player props. Third, the EPA likelihood kernel serves as the fundamental reward function. It quantifies the marginal value of any single play based on down, distance, and field position. This kernel is the building block for all higher-order efficiency metrics. The dualities emerge when mapping these distinct methodologies—process-oriented betting, fantasy optimization, and contextual journalism—into a unified probabilistic framework. Failure modes arise when these models assume stationarity during structural breaks, such as sudden quarterback changes or rule modifications, causing the inferred parameters to diverge rapidly from reality.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: These primitives trace back to the foundational work of Dean Oliver in basketball analytics ('For the Win'), which introduced advanced efficiency metrics. In football, this evolved through the adoption of Expected Points Added (EPA) by researchers like Ben Baldwin and the Any Given Sunday analytics community. The shift from descriptive statistics to predictive, process-oriented modeling was heavily influenced by the application of poker theory and dynamic programming to sports betting, popularized by figures like Rufus Peabody and Ed Miller.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Modeling opposing agents in this ecosystem involves understanding the distinct objectives of various actors. The independent analyst seeks to maximize predictive accuracy to build reputation and sell subscriptions. The sportsbook aims to balance the book and minimize exposure to sharp money. The recreational bettor often chases narrative-driven outcomes rather than probabilistic edges. Our GSI/GSE engines must anticipate how these actors will react to public information releases, effectively modeling a multi-agent game where information asymmetry dictates market movements.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent model collapse, strict anti-collinearity vetoes must be enforced. For instance, if the EPA likelihood kernel is highly correlated with simple yards gained due to a lack of situational weighting, the derived efficiency metrics become redundant. Furthermore, leakage vetoes ensure that future simulation results (e.g., post-injury projections) do not inadvertently contaminate the training data for historical baseline models. We must also veto the direct application of fantasy-focused truncated distributions to team-total betting markets without appropriate scaling factors, as the aggregation of individual variances does not linearly map to team-level outcomes.
